neighbours.label: ' higher', ' greater' or ' more' straight after a stated multiple or percentage ('50 percent higher', '13-fold higher'), or ' majority' after 'slight', as opposed to the same comparative with no amount
fire: Drivers under 25 face a 30 percent higher risk of a crash.
Women in the trial showed a 4-fold greater response to the vaccine.
Northern farms reported 12 percent higher yields than southern ones.
Users of the new filter had a 20% lower error rate than the rest.
A narrow majority of voters backed the plan in the spring.
Trees in the plot grew about 15 percent taller in wet years.
The enzyme has a roughly 8-fold higher affinity for glucose.
Graduates earn nearly 40 percent more over a working life.
quiet: Drivers under 25 pay a higher price for a crash.
Women in the trial showed a far greater response to the vaccine.
Northern farms reported higher yields than southern ones.
Users of the new filter had a lower error rate than the rest.
A large crowd of voters backed the plan in the spring.
Trees in the plot grew a bit taller in wet years.
The enzyme has an unusually high affinity for glucose.
Graduates earn quite a bit more over a working life.

short: comparative after a percentage or multiple
notes: 'Lower', 'taller' and 'narrow majority' extend the probed cases and were not probed themselves.
